Lucerastat, an oral therapy for Fabry disease: results from a pivotal randomized phase 3 study and its open-label extension * Article * Open access * Published: 10 January 2026 # Lucerastat, an oral therapy for Fabry disease: results from a pivotal randomized phase 3 study and its open-label extension Nature Communications volume 17, Article number: 1534 (2026) ## Abstract In Fabry disease (FD, OMIM #301500), a rare lysosomal storage disorder, the glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor lucerastat acts as substrate reduction therapy. The Phase 3, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 6-month, randomized clinical trial, MODIFY (NCT03425539), aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of lucerastat in adults with FD with moderate-to-severe neuropathic pain. The single-arm, open-label extension (OLE) (NCT03737214) evaluated the longer-term safety and tolerability of lucerastat over 72 months. Lucerastat 1000 mg twice daily (n = 80), compared with placebo (n = 37), failed to affect neuropathic pain at Month-6, with no significant difference between treatment groups (LSM difference –0.42 [95% CI –1.23, 0.40], p = 0.32) (primary endpoint). In contrast, a decrease in baseline plasma Gb3 was observed at Month-6 in lucerastat-treated participants but not placebo-treated participants (LSM difference –873.53 ng/mL [95% CI –1097.53, –649.53], p < 0.0001; NS due to hierarchical testing). In an unplanned OLE Month-18 interim analysis, the eGFR slope (mL/min/1.73m^{2}/year) in 93 participants with pre- and post-randomization (23-month median lucerastat exposure) eGFR data was –3.50 (–5.04, –1.969) and –1.48 (–2.64, –0.33), respectively. Lucerastat was safe and well tolerated. Lucerastat’s strong pharmacodynamic effect did not translate into an effect on neuropathic pain. The potential effect of lucerastat on renal function requires further investigation (Trial registration NCT03425539, NCT03737214; 2017-003369-85, 2018-002210-12. The studies were sponsored by Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd). -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Idorsia | Lucerastat (https://www.idorsia.com/our-innovation/portfolio/lucerastat.html) citeturn359search2 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; As the next steps in the Phase 3 program are underway, the OLE study was concluded and participants still receiving lucerastat at study closure were moved to a post-trial access program ensuring continuity of care. ... The broader FDA-aligned Phase 3 program will also include a 74-patient comparative renal function study, FAB-SWITCH, evaluating lucerastat against standard-of-care enzyme replacement therapies, designed to establish lucerastat as the first oral therapy addressing the full spectrum of Fabry patients. ## Current status In October 2026, Idorsia initiated FAB-KLEAR the pivotal Phase 3 kidney biopsy study of lucerastat in adult patients with Fabry disease. FAB-KLEAR is an open-label study that will enroll 16 treatment naïve or pseudo naïve adult male patients with Fabry disease. The study is designed to assess the potential for lucerastat to reduce kidney Gb3 accumulation, a key driver of Fabry-related kidney disease, through the primary endpoint of change from baseline to Month 18 in kidney Gb3 BLISS score (average number of Gb3 inclusions per kidney peritubular capillary (PTC)). A decrease from baseline to Month 18 in kidney Gb3 BLISS score indicates a reduction in the average number of Gb3 inclusions per peritubular capillary and therefore evidence of a histological treatment effect on kidney Gb3. The study will also measure the change from baseline to Month 18 in plasma Gb3 concentration, as well as assessing the safety and pharmacokinetic profile of lucerastat. The broader FDA-aligned Phase 3 program will also include a 74-patient comparative renal function study, FAB-SWITCH, evaluating lucerastat against standard-of-care enzyme replacement therapies, designed to establish lucerastat as the first oral therapy addressing the full spectrum of Fabry patients. Together, these complementary studies are expected to support a regulatory filing as early as 2029. Idorsia has aligned the development strategy of the Phase 3 program with the US FDA. The design of the program is also consistent with feedback received from the European Medicines Agency during previous regulatory interactions. ### Milestones 2026    FAB-KLEAR study initiated 2026    New data and evaluation of long-term treatment                                                                         with lucerastat presented at WORLDSymposium™ 2026 2021    Phase 3 open label extension study continued 2021    Phase 3 study completed – primary endpoint not met 2018     Phase 3 study initiated 2016    Phase 1b study completed ### Key scientific literature * Nordbeck P., et al.
